title: feat(types,fields): formula and summary widgets read the spec's returnType and summaryOperations; field metadata retires the snake spellings (objectui#11070, round 3)
body:
Refs #11070
Clause-②: yes (narrowing). The form-field face declares the spec's `returnType` and `summaryOperations` (the strict accept set widens by those two keys), while a malformed value for either is now refused by the tolerant face too, and `FormulaFieldMetadata` / `SummaryFieldMetadata` / `PasswordFieldMetadata` retire their snake_case members (the published TypeScript types narrow), under the startup no-gradualism rule. Both directions were measured on the built face at base and head (below), and the changeset prices the break as minor.

`Refs`, not a closing keyword, on purpose: the card keeps its remainder after this lands (the grid field's `columns`, the `object-chart` declaration, the dashboard pairs per objectui#11228, and the `reference_to` stop below). This is round 3 of the card, executing the seat's answers Q2 A and Q3 A (`5914385802`) under claim `5915152317`. Draft; the dev does not mark it ready.

## What changed

- **Form-field face (`@object-ui/types`).** `FormField` declares `returnType?: SpecField['returnType']` and `summaryOperations?: SpecField['summaryOperations']`; the zod mirror `FormFieldSchema` declares `stripImportedDefaults(SpecFieldSchema).shape.returnType` / `.summaryOperations`. Both are the spec's `FieldSchema` members by reference, never a restated copy. `form-field-zod-coverage` gains the two keys.
- **Widgets (`@object-ui/fields`).** `FormulaField` reads `returnType` only (`number` to two decimals, `boolean` as Yes/No, `date` through the shared date face, else text). `SummaryField` reads `summaryOperations.function` only (`count` as it arrives; `sum` / `avg` / `min` / `max` to two decimals). The snake_case reads are gone, with no alias and no dual read. `FormulaField`'s `currency` branch is gone as well: the spec's `returnType` does not list `currency`.
- **Field metadata types (`@object-ui/types`, `field-types.ts`).** `FormulaFieldMetadata.return_type` becomes `returnType`; `SummaryFieldMetadata.summary_object` / `summary_field` / `summary_type` become `summaryOperations` (`object` / `field` / `function`); `PasswordFieldMetadata.min_length` / `max_length` become `minLength` / `maxLength`. Each new member is `SpecField['KEY']`. `SummaryFieldMetadata.summary_filter` also becomes `summaryOperations.filter`, under the bounded in-place exemption (same defect class and same interface; a mechanical fold whose target shape the spec pins; the file is this claim's; no new verification surface). Nothing reads `summary_filter`, and leaving it would have kept a second spelling of `filter` beside `summaryOperations`.
- **Fixtures.** `fields-formula/*` write the spec's `expression` and `returnType`; `fields-summary/*` fold `summary_object` / `summary_field` / `summary_type` into `summaryOperations { object, field, function }`. The `fields-lookup` and `fields-password` fixtures already wrote `reference` / `minLength` (round 1).
- **Tests.** The five `packages/fields` tests that rendered `FormulaField` with `return_type: 'date'` write `returnType: 'date'`, now as annotated literals (the `as any` cast is gone, so `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json` judges the key). A new pin, `widgets/__tests__/formula-summary-spec-reads-11070.test.tsx`, covers both widgets' spec reads, each against a control that changes only that key, plus the retirement (a snake spelling alone formats nothing). `strict-face-read-keys-11070.test.ts` accepts the two keys, refuses bad values on both faces, moves `return_type` / `summary_type` from PENDING to RETIRED (with `summary_object` / `summary_field`), and adds type-level pins: the members equal the spec's exactly, and the retired names are gone from the three metadata types.
- **Ledger rows the declarations move, and only those.** `zod-mirror-parity`'s `UNNAMED_LAZY_SLOTS` records `form.zod.ts#FormFieldSchema.summaryOperations`: its `filter` is the spec's recursive filter condition, a `z.lazy` inside an imported schema. `imported-defaults-8317`'s comment no longer states a member count. No parity key set or total moved.
- **Docs.** `fields/formula.mdx`, `fields/summary.mdx` and `fields/password.mdx` teach the spec members in their typed fences, their plaintext fences and their prose (including the summary page's backend sketch).
- **Changeset.** `.changeset/11070-field-metadata-spec-spellings.md`: `@object-ui/types` and `@object-ui/fields` **minor**, with the break stated (AGENTS.md: the fixed group never declares major). Three pending entries this change makes false get a dated note, appended in the maintainer's shape: `6138-fields-schema-block-parity-pr2.md` (the shipped `return_type` union), `8194-fields-date-widget-convention.md` and `8809-date-carrier-unparsable.md` (`return_type: 'date'`).

## Stopped: `reference_to` (the ruling's live-producer case)

The brief's stop rule says not to retire a spelling a live producer still writes, and to stop at that key. `reference_to` has live producers inside this repository, so `LookupFieldMetadata.reference_to`, `MasterDetailFieldMetadata.reference_to`, the lookup readers' `reference_to` limb, `lookup.mdx` and its fixtures are **untouched**. H2 holds: `MetadataProvider`'s comment is a read (`d.reference ?? d.reference_to`), and the writers are these.

| writer (production source) | package | writes `reference_to` onto |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `normalizeFieldReferenceKeys` (the ingestion stamp) | core | every ingested object field definition with a target (`MetadataProvider`'s list and by-name reads, `ObjectStackAdapter.getObjectSchema`) |
| `paramToField` | app-shell | an action parameter's lookup field |
| `RecordDetailView` (`toField`) | app-shell | detail section fields |
| `FlowReferenceField` | app-shell | the `field` prop of `LookupField`, a typed `LookupFieldMetadata` literal |
| `RecordDetailPanel` | plugin-detail | `DetailViewField`, whose contract declares `reference_to` |
| `RecordMetaFooter` | plugin-detail | the lookup cell renderer's field |
| `RelatedList` | plugin-detail | a typed `FieldMetadata` literal |
| `fieldEnrichment`, `buildDefaultPageSchema` | plugin-detail | enriched and synthesized field definitions |
| `sectionFields` | plugin-form | a section field's override |
| `bulkParamToField` | plugin-grid | a bulk-action parameter field |
| `ObjectGallery` | plugin-list | enriched field definitions |

The three readers that would lose the limb are `LookupField` (`reference_to || reference`), `UserField` (`reference || reference_to`) and `LookupCellRenderer` (`reference_to || reference`). The pending `.changeset/6837-reference-to-arm-deletion.md` records leaving exactly those three alone for this reason. objectstack's example apps (objectstack `origin/main` `00a92e18d`) write `reference_to` 0 times. Retiring it means retiring ObjectUI's own internal carrier spelling across six packages; that is the maintainer question in the report, not this PR.

## Runtime probe: an object-bound formula and summary field, before and after

A scratch test (never committed) rendered `ObjectForm` in edit mode with a stub data source. `getObjectSchema` returned field definitions exactly as objectstack's example apps write them: app-todo's `days_overdue` (`returnType: 'number'`), app-crm's `line_total` (`summaryOperations: { object, field, function: 'sum' }`), plus a boolean formula, a date formula and a `count` roll-up. `findOne` returned the record. The base leg swapped in the two widget files' base blobs (hash equal to base verified) and restored them (blob equal to HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty).

| field, as the example apps write it | value | base `0c95d3d` | head |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| formula, `returnType: 'number'` | `3` | `3` | `3.00` |
| formula, `returnType: 'boolean'` | `true` | `true` | `Yes` |
| formula, `returnType: 'date'` | `2026-07-04` | `2026-07-04` | `Jul 4` |
| summary, `function: 'sum'` | `15750.5` | `15750.5` | `15750.50` |
| summary, `function: 'count'` (control) | `4` | `4` | `4` |

The type formatting did not apply on an object-bound form before, and it does now. This is the user-visible half of the round.

## Census

**Type-checker census of the retired members.** A TypeScript LanguageService `findReferences` from each member's declaration, run at base `0c95d3d`. The program was every tracked TS/TSX file that names one of the member names (223 files), under the root `tsconfig` (its `paths` map `@object-ui/types` to source), with the other packages' types resolved from built `dist`.

| member | typed references outside the declaration |
| --- | --: |
| `FormulaFieldMetadata.return_type` | 0 |
| `SummaryFieldMetadata.summary_object` / `summary_field` / `summary_type` / `summary_filter` | 0 each |
| `PasswordFieldMetadata.min_length` / `max_length` | 0 each |
| `LookupFieldMetadata.reference_to` (the live control, and the stop case) | 8 writes: `FlowReferenceField`, `RelatedList`, 6 test literals |
| `MasterDetailFieldMetadata.reference_to` | 1 write: `RelatedList` |

A first run without built dists missed `FlowReferenceField` (its `LookupField` import resolved to nothing), so the reading above is the run with them. The untyped reads, found by grep because `any` hides them from the type checker, are these. `return_type` is read by `FormulaField` and written by the five `fields` tests through `as any`. `summary_type` is read by `SummaryField`. `min_length` / `max_length` are read only by the generic `minLength ?? min_length` readers: `buildValidationRules`, `ObjectForm`, `EmbeddableForm`, the form renderer's input / textarea / fallback branches, `RichTextField` and `TextAreaField`. Those serve every text-family type, and none is password-specific; `PasswordField` reads neither. **So the package set is `@object-ui/types` and `@object-ui/fields`.** Every package that names the changed or newly typed members was type-checked as well: `core`, `components`, `plugin-designer`, `plugin-form`, `app-shell` and `example-schema-catalog`.

**M3, before and after.** Round 2's method: a port of PR objectui#11069's `findUndeclaredKeys` plus `measure-strict-authoring-face.mjs`'s loaders and node walk, run over the SHIPPED face from a freshly built `packages/types/dist` in each tree.

| reading | base `0c95d3d` | head `2a83d35` |
| --- | --: | --: |
| node documents | 599 | 599 |
| refused by the strict face | 96 | 93 |
| of them strict-only | 60 | 57 |
| refused by the tolerant face | 36 | 36 |
| **class (ii)** pairs / occurrences / strict-only | **12 / 53 / 53** | **10 / 47 / 47** |

Every pair that moved is listed. `form · fields[].return_type` 3 → 0 and `summary_type` 3 → 0 leave class (ii). `summary_object` 3 → 0 and `summary_field` 3 → 0 leave class (i). `form · fields[].formula` 3 → 0 becomes `form · fields[].expression` 0 → 3, a lateral move inside class (i): the spec formula key, which nothing on the form path reads and `FormField` does not declare (see Acceptance notes). The 10 pairs left are the 9 dashboard pairs and the grid field's `columns`. H3 holds for its first half. Its second half, the doc-taught `reference_to` / `min_length`, had nothing to lose: M3 reads only JSON documents and JSON fences, and neither key occurs there at base. The `password.mdx` TypeScript fence is judged by `check:doc-snippets` instead (below).

**Accept sets, measured on the built face at base and head.**

| document (a `form` field) | base tolerant / strict | head tolerant / strict |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `returnType: 'number'` | accept / refuse | accept / accept |
| `summaryOperations: { object, field, function: 'sum' }` | accept / refuse | accept / accept |
| `returnType: 'datetime'` | accept / refuse | refuse / refuse |
| `summaryOperations` with no `function`, with `function: 'first'`, or with an unknown member | accept / refuse | refuse / refuse |
| `return_type: 'number'`, `summary_type: 'sum'` | accept / refuse | accept / refuse |

Type-aware linting is not enabled in `eslint.config.js` (`tseslint.configs.recommended`, no parser project), so the diff cannot move a verdict on an untouched file |

The pending changesets `check:changeset-claims` names for files this change edits (30 of them) were read. None states anything about the members this change moves, apart from the three with a dated note.

**Reverse verification.** Each ablation was committed first, predicted before the run, and applied through objectstack's `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`: the anchor hit once, the blob moved, and the restore left the blob equal to HEAD with `git diff HEAD` empty.

| ablation | predicted | measured |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A1 `FormulaField` reads `return_type` again | the new pin's 3 formula cases red; every `FormulaField` row of the five date files red; summary green | 35 red / 190 green: 3 in the pin, 32 `FormulaField` rows, no other row |
| A2 `SummaryField` reads `summary_type` again | 5 red (sum / avg / min / max and the retirement case) | 5 red / 4 green |
| A3 zod `FormFieldSchema.returnType` deleted | 3 red (strict-face acceptance, `datetime` refused on both faces, coverage exact set) plus `tsc` red | 3 red / 83 green; `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json` exit 2 (TS2322 in the parity ledger) |

| A5 `formula.mdx`'s typed fence writes `return_type` again | `check:doc-snippets` 1 failed, proving the gate judged the rebuilt `dist` | exit 1 · `696 of 696 block(s) judged, 1 failed` · TS2561 naming `return_type` ("Did you mean to write 'returnType'?") |

NOT MEASURED locally, left to CI: the repository-wide lint and test shards beyond the named sets; the Spec Main Shape Gate; `type-check` of the downstream packages that name none of the changed members.

## Acceptance notes

- **The formula fixtures are still strict-refused, now for `expression`.** The ruling moved them to the spec formula key. `FormField` does not declare `expression`, and nothing on the hand-authored form path reads it (the value is computed by the backend), so it is class (i), the same as `formula` before. The three summary fixtures now parse on the strict face. Round 1 dropped the auto-number fixtures' `format` for the same reason. Whether to drop `expression` from these three fixtures is in the report.
- **`FormulaFieldMetadata.formula` is the spec's `expression` under another name.** The spec refuses `formula` by name, with a rename hint to `expression`. The type still declares `formula`, so `formula.mdx`'s typed fence still teaches it. `formula` also has readers outside this claim (app-shell's metadata admin reads `def.expression ?? def.formula`, and plugin-form's `sanitize` reads `fieldDef.formula`). This is the same snake-versus-spec family, left for the card's remainder.
- **The other text-family metadata types still declare `min_length` / `max_length`** (`Text`, `Textarea`, `Markdown`, `Html`, `Richtext`, `Email` and `Url`), and their pages teach them. They have live dual readers. Same family, outside Q3's ruling, which named `PasswordFieldMetadata`.
- `auto_compute` / `auto_update` stay declared. Nothing reads them, but neither is a snake twin of a spec member, so they are noted here only.
